sections.text: Then the experience acquired in his former life will revive, and with its help he will strive for perfection more eagerly than before.
Unconsciously he will return to the practices of his old life; so that he who tries to realise spiritual consciousness is certainly superior to one who only talks of it.
Then after many lives, the student of spirituality, who earnestly strives, and whose sins are absolved, attains perfection and reaches the Supreme.

So we had been discussing Chapter 6, Dhyana Yoga, Yoga of Meditation and we are coming to the conclusion of this chapter. We are also coming to the conclusion of the first segment of Bhagavad Gita. As we had discussed many times before, Bhagavad Gita is divided into three segments.
First six chapters deal with who I am at this limited being as an individual. Next six chapters will deal with who that ultimate reality is. The last three chapters will deal with how you can synchronize these two.
So we are coming to the end of the first segment of Bhagavad Gita and what we have learned so far is in the chapter one we have learnt about our own situation, that our situation is not clear cut in life. Things dont come in life as clear as black and white. It comes in various shades of gray.
That was the first chapter, Arjuna Vishada Yoga that confuses us. Chapter two gave us a thumbnail sketch the entire knowledge of Bhagavad Gita, Upanishada and Brahma Sutra. What is reality and what is perceived to be my reality? Right now I consider myself to be mortal.
I had a beginning and Ill have an end. And the elder Bhagwan said, your self is imperishable, immutable. We have come to this stage by passing through many, many experiences in different states of existence.
Chapters three through five gave us instruction on how to optimize our performance in this life using the equipment we have -- dealing with the cards we are dealt. How do you optimize your game? That was the topic of chapter third through fifth. And chapter six gave us the instruction how to now raise your plateau.
Im comfortable dealing in this sphere. How do I now go a step above that? You may be a local level politician going through the school board elections. Then I want to do at the state level.
Then I want to do at a national level. Well, how do I raise my plateau is the topic of chapter 6, Dhyana Yoga Yoga of meditation. All my focus right now is this body, this mind, this intellect and this world.
Now how do I conduct transaction in this world and how do I optimize it? Thats what we have learned. Chapter six is, now that you have learned how to optimize your performance in this world, go to the next level of finding out what is the real nature of the self is there was meditation. We have learned in this process that there are two ways to get there.
The one who gives up the fruits of actions is a Karma Yogi. The one who gives up the sense of agency -- I am the doer -- is a Sannyasi. Both reach the same goal of realizing the truth, the self.
That changes my identification from this limited being to that unlimited self. So we have elaborate discussion about how to meditate. And then we have come to the last portion of it where Arjuna had two doubts.
First is we are talking about controlling our mind. My experience so far is mind is so fickle. Controlling it doesnt seem like an achievable goal.
And Bhagavan said it can be done by Abhyasa in Vairagya, by constant practice, by forming a habit. Once you form a habit, it becomes very easy, automatic. So thats Abhyasa and Vairagya.
To form a habit in one sphere, you have to undo your habits in the other sphere -- that is Vairagya. You have to give up what you are attached to right now in order to do something else. Then Arjuna had the second doubt: I sincerely try all these things, but then I run out of time. Then what happens to all my efforts? Will that be all in vain? That I have lost on both hands? That I have not enjoyed my life here in the material world? And also Im not making any progress in my spiritual evolution.
In response to that, we have seen that the concept of reincarnation was reintroduced in this chapter. Where I am today is the sum total of all my experiences before. What Im doing with my total experiences now in my present today, that will make my future.
This life is a continuum. This existence is a continuum. Whether I exist in this form or the other.
When I was born, I was a baby. I existed as a baby for a while, then as a teenager, then as a young man. But I exist all through this.
So will you exist in your future state of existence we call a rebirth. And there he gives us assurance. Fruits of all your efforts will be with you.
You will carry your bank balance. If I retire from my practice here and leave the United States and go to India, what will happen to all my bank balance? It will come with you. It will be transferable.
You can convert it into rupees. So all that we have done will come with us in our next life. Thats the assurance.
So the last few verses which you have seen say that the Yogi who had been striving to achieve this but cannot come see, falls from his path for whatever reason, runs out of time, get distracted. He said then he will get a place in his next birthday in a conducive environment. Suchinam srimatam Gehei.
He will take birth in the house of a pure and wealthy. So he will have conducive environment to pursue his path. This is what he will then go and fulfill all his desires.
Bhagavan guarantees that all your desires will be fulfilled sooner or later. As long as you have a strong desire to achieve something, to experience something, you will achieve it sooner or later. Most of the things I wanted to do in my 20s, I finally got it in 60s.
So it takes that much time. But you will be the assurance is all your desires will be fulfilled. You will have time to exhaust them.
Then continue pursuing your path again. That if the Yogi had some desires left to pursue, but those who have no desire, they purely in the path of this yoga, but ran out of time. He said they will take birth in a home of a yogi where the utmost was conducive for him to start his journey right away, to continue on his path.
And then the last few verses talks about what will happen once you take that next birth. Tatratam buddhi sahyogam labate Parva DEI kam. Parva dehikam in the last life, the knowledge which you have gathered through your efforts in yoga, in meditation, in a Karma yoga, whatever practice you have done.
This is also true for all our secular efforts. Thats why we have talked about child prodigies, musical geniuses, mathematical geniuses. Our culture doesnt consider these an accident or random happening.
Its a systematic evolution of that intellect to come to that point. They say he gets Buddhi Samyogam -- he gets associated with the buddhi he developed in his last birth. Yatate cha tatah bhuyah samsiddhau Kuru Nandana -- and then he strives even more than before, because now he gets even more encouraged by his own accomplishments, his own prowess.
The child who is good at mathematics will be more encouraged to learn more and more quickly because he gets encouraged by his own success. Nothing succeeds like success and nothing fails like failure. Once you get this taste of success, you go more and more -- so there, Yatate, striving even more than before.
He will achieve that perfection. Kuru Nandana -- so he addresses Arjuna as Kuru Nandana. You are the son of the Kuru dynasty.
Remind them how did you come to this jackpot that you were born in a Kuru dynasty as a prince because of your past karmas. You and I constantly question why I have this situation, and the others have better situation than I. But we never question why I have better situation than those who do not.
We have come to this situation by our own efforts. Hinduism doesnt give any other choice but to put all the responsibilities on you. You are the architect of your own destiny, even your parents.
You have chosen yourself as per our scriptures. Which house will I buy when I move out from my current house? Whatever the bank balance I have created and what the neighbor, I think will be the best. Thats where Im going to go and buy a house, right? There may be hundreds of other nice neighbors.
I never knew about it or never thought they would be conducive for me. I go to some of these farmhouses and really wonder why people want to live here. One it looks so scary for miles.
You know, theres nobody if something happens at night to take a grocery or drive probably another 20 miles to buy a grocery. But they say, no, no, we live in farmhouse because thats what that person thought is the right way to live for me. Put me in the densest neighborhood and Ill be very, very happy.
So each one of us decides what is best for us. And that is what Bhagavan gives. Bhagavan is so compassionate.
So there he says, in your new situation you will be associated with your intellect, which you are gathered in the Pavadaya in your past existence. And there you will try even more to achieve the perfection, reminding Arjuna and all of us, how did we come to this stage because of our past effort, why we are in Gita group and not in some other place. Because your own efforts you gathered this interest to learn Bhagavad Gita.
The next verse says: Purva abhyasena tena eva hriyate hi avashah api sah, jijnasuh api yogasya shabda brahma ativartate. By that very former practice he is born with -- in spite of himself, in spite of whatever the circumstances are -- because of purva abhyasa, by your previous experiences and studies, you will make progress. When Mohandas Gandhi left India to go to London for his studies, what did his mother say? You will not eat meat.
You will not do this. That was the fear: when you leave your country, you will be influenced by the other culture and forget your own culture, your own values, your own traditions. But look whats happening here. We have more Gita classes and Bala Vihar classes in this country than when I was growing up in India.
There were no Gita classes then. Because of your own vasanas, you continue wherever you go.: somebodys parents came and he was very worried. How will I keep my father engaged after all? I found out that his father himself found a company in the neighborhood because he was great at Tinpathi.
He somehow, whether he speaks English or not, he found people in the neighborhood who plays Tinpathi and he made his friends by himself. With your own vasanas, you will find your own environment to fit in. In spite of whatever environment you are in, you will strive harder, and jijnasuh api -- with curiosity about yoga -- asking What is that perfection which I need to achieve? Yogasya shabda brahma ativartate -- with that yoga, he will go beyond Shabda Brahma.
Now, these final few verses are actually the preface to the next chapter, where you will be introduced to the concept of Shabda Brahma. We all have learned that in our culture the sound symbol of God is Om.

Verse 43 describes what happens after a spiritually inclined person takes a new birth: Tatra tam buddhi-samyogam labhate paurva-dehikam - there, that person regains connection with the intelligence developed in the previous body. This explains the phenomenon we see: some people are inexplicably drawn to spiritual seeking from early childhood, while others with every advantage show no such inclination. The draw comes from within - from previous development - not from external circumstances alone.
The remarkable statement in verse 44 - Purvaabhyasena tenaiva hriyate hy avashopi sah - emphasizes that one is carried forward by previous practice, even against ones conscious will. Parents feared their son would lose his culture in a foreign land, but instead, more Gita classes flourish in America than in India. A father visiting from abroad, speaking little English, spontaneously finds friends who play Tinpathi because that is his vasana seeking expression. Your deeper tendencies will find their outlet regardless of external circumstances.
Verse 45 gives the long view: Aneka-janma-samsiddhas tato yati param gatim - perfected through many births, one finally reaches the supreme goal. This is not discouraging but realistic. We would not expect to master any great skill in a single attempt; why expect instant enlightenment? Today, reflect on your own spiritual tendencies. What aspects of the practice feel natural, as if you are remembering rather than learning? What draws you to these teachings? Trust that these inclinations are not random but reflect your souls ongoing journey. Continue practicing with faith that nothing is lost and everything contributes to eventual attainment.
